You added a new learning loop the right way — a `blueprints/<id>/blueprint.yaml`
with `singleton: true` (and maybe `singletonActive: true`), a deterministic op
registered in `blueprint-steps/index.ts`, an entry in `LEARNING_SINGLETONS`, a
flag defaulting ON. It type-checks, the blueprint test passes, it ships to green.
And then… nothing fires. It is not in `improvements:learning_loops`. Its output
table stays empty forever.

**Why:** adding the blueprint ships only the loop's *definition*. The actual
`harness_shared.routines` row — `@singleton/bp-singleton-<id>-0`, the thing the
routine engine ticks — is **never created on deploy or operator boot**. There is
no boot-time materializer that walks `LEARNING_SINGLETONS` and upserts rows.
`materializeLearningSingletons` / `materializeBlueprintTriggers` is called only
from:

- the **seed CLI** (`packages/operator-core/lib/blueprint/seed-learning-singletons.ts`),
  run by hand, and
- `enable-platform-mode.ts` (when the owner first enables platform mode — it
  flips the `PLATFORM_IMPROVEMENT_LOOPS` flag ON **first**, then calls
  `materializeLearningSingletons` so Class-C singletons actually get written), and
- `harness:create` / `pot:create` (for that harness's own blueprint, not the
  workspace singletons).

**P-070 deployment-mode gate (added 2026-06-14):** `materializeLearningSingletons`
now has a skip condition for Class-C platform-improvement loops: if the
`PLATFORM_IMPROVEMENT_LOOPS` flag is OFF (a public release or a fresh install
before the owner enables platform mode), the seed CLI prints:

```
SKIP <id>: platform-improvement loops are OFF (PLATFORM_IMPROVEMENT_LOOPS) — release/non-platform mode (P-070)
```

and creates **no `@singleton` row** — not even a dark/inactive one. `--execute`
returns without an error; the loop is simply not materialized. In dev/self-host
the flag defaults ON so this gate is transparent, but on a clean install or a
release image it is the silent barrier. Fix: enable platform mode first
(`enablePlatformMode` / the owner's platform-mode toggle) — that flips the flag ON,
then materializes all Class-C singletons atomically. If you are seeding manually
on a release box, verify the flag is ON before running `--execute`.

So the existing live loops (calibration, scout, iq-battery, …) got their
`@singleton` rows from a **past owner-run seed campaign**, not from their code
landing. A brand-new loop inherits none of that.

**Fix — materialize it once, AFTER your code is deployed to the operator that
runs the routine engine** (the routine fires `system:blueprint-run`, which loads
your blueprint + op on the *running* operator; do it before the code is there and
the first fire fails to resolve):

```sh
# dry-run first (prints the plan, writes nothing)
PAPERCUSP_WORKSPACE_ID=<ws> DATABASE_URL=… \
  npx tsx packages/operator-core/lib/blueprint/seed-learning-singletons.ts --only <id>
# then create the @singleton row
… --only <id> --execute
```

`singletonActive: true` makes it seed **active** (always-on monitoring, e.g.
iq-battery / memory-precision); `false` (the frontier default) seeds it **dark**,
still needing the three arming gates afterward. Either way the ROW must exist
first.

This is the **0th gate**, before the three in
[[dark-learning-loops-are-triple-gated]]: routine row exists → routine active →
flag ON → governor budgeted. A flag default-ON and a green deploy are necessary
but **not sufficient** — without the materialize step the loop has no heartbeat
at all.

(Two smaller traps seen alongside, 2026-06-18: the `papercup-staging-api`
:3170 instance runs `PAPERCUSP_DBOS_ROUTINES=0` and does **not** boot-apply
migrations — restarting it won't apply a new `sql/NNN-*.sql`; that happens on the
main operator's boot after the file reaches its checkout. And when you build a
bench to MONITOR an already-floored metric, replay the gold set **with** the
production floor — `runGoldSet(…, { minScore, minLexScore })` — not the unfloored
`runBench`, or you measure raw-recall FP@5 (~100%) instead of the floored
production number (~17%).)
